newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore dlr breaks through 1.40 on MAS comments.
newsitem.headline: Singapore dlr breaks through 1.40 on MAS comments.

text.p: The Singapore dollar dashed up through the psychological 1.40-mark against the U.S. dollar on Friday after Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) officials said its policy on the local currency remained unchanged.
By 0610 GMT, the Sing stood at 1.3980 per dollar, from around 1.4015 at the morning.
The Sing last traded above 1.40 on February 21 this year.
Dealers said the market had taken as bullish for the Sing a statement by the MAS that it still wanted to internationalise the currency, but gradually.

One currency analyst said the immediate break had followed publication on Reuters of a report on the MAS comments which were made earlier on Friday morning at Singapore's third quarter economic briefing.
The head of treasury at a European bank said once the 1.40-level had been breached, other buying followed quickly.
"The move was very sudden. The reason it was so quick was a lot of stop-losses were triggered," he said.
The Malaysian ringgit fell to a low of 0.5547 against the Sing at the same time, breaking through previous strong support at 0.5555.
